header.contentArea: Practical procedures: radial arterial blood gas sampling
guidelineVersions: Resuscitation Council UK, The ABCDE Approach (last updated July 2024)
Health and Safety (Sharp Instruments in Healthcare) Regulations 2013

related.why: Interpreting the arterial blood gas result this station's sample would produce
Another aseptic vascular-access procedural station: ultrasound-guided central venous catheter insertion

brief.scenario: Ms Grace Harmsworth, 69, has worsening breathlessness and needs an arterial blood gas.
brief.task: Perform radial arterial blood gas sampling safely on a manikin, talking the examiner through each step.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Consent and check, then a clean, safe puncture, then handle the sample and yourself safely.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Rushing to needle the wrist before confirming identity, consent and bleeding risk.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'll confirm her identity, explain the procedure and gain consent before I start."

grid.label: Consent and identification
grid.fail: Proceeds without confirming identity or gaining consent.
grid.pass: Confirms patient identity, explains the indication and procedure, and gains consent.
grid.high: Checks the patient understands why the sample is needed and what it will show, and offers to answer questions before proceeding.

grid.label: Safety check before puncture
grid.fail: Does not ask about anticoagulation, bleeding risk or local contraindications.
grid.pass: Checks anticoagulation/bleeding risk and any local contraindications to radial puncture before proceeding.
grid.high: Explains that a formal Allen test is not universally required when collateral circulation is otherwise clinically adequate, and follows local policy rather than treating it as a fixed rule.

grid.label: Aseptic preparation and technique
grid.fail: Skips hand hygiene or skin preparation, or contaminates the needle/syringe.
grid.pass: Positions the wrist comfortably, identifies the radial pulse, prepares equipment and uses aseptic technique, with local anaesthetic where appropriate.
grid.high: Explains the choice of needle angle and technique for the self-filling syringe, and adapts positioning if the pulse is difficult to locate rather than repeatedly stabbing blindly.

grid.label: Safe puncture and sample collection
grid.fail: Repeatedly punctures the artery without stopping to reassess or seek help.
grid.pass: Palpates the artery, inserts the needle with an appropriate angle, allows arterial blood to fill the syringe without forcing it, then removes the needle safely.
grid.high: Recognises early when a puncture is unsuccessful, stops, reassesses landmarks or asks for senior help rather than persisting.

grid.label: Sample handling and documentation
grid.fail: Sends an unlabelled sample, or fails to record the oxygen therapy/device.
grid.pass: Mixes the sample per the device instructions, labels it, analyses it promptly, and documents the oxygen therapy or device and FiO2 at the time of sampling.
grid.high: Explains why oxygen therapy must be recorded: pulse oximetry does not detect hypercapnia, so the inspired oxygen and SpO2 both need documenting to interpret the gas correctly.

grid.label: Aftercare, sharps safety and disposal (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Fails to apply pressure afterwards, or disposes of the needle unsafely.
grid.pass: Applies firm pressure until haemostasis is achieved, disposes of sharps safely at the point of use, and assesses the puncture site and distal circulation.
grid.high: States pressure needs to be longer if the patient is anticoagulated, and interprets the result alongside the clinical picture once available.

fail.text: Perform an arterial blood gas from the radial artery.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'll just get the syringe ready and find the pulse.

fail.text: Have you checked anything about her first?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Not really, I'll just go for the wrist.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Perform an arterial blood gas from the radial artery.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'll confirm her identity, explain the procedure and the reason for it, and gain her consent first.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Anything you'd check before you start?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Whether she's anticoagulated or has a bleeding risk, and any local contraindication to using this wrist.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'll position her wrist comfortably, locate the radial pulse, prepare my equipment and use an aseptic technique, with local anaesthetic if appropriate.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'll palpate the artery, insert the needle at an appropriate angle, and let the syringe fill on its own rather than pulling back forcefully. Then I'll withdraw the needle safely.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What do you do with the sample?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Mix it as the device instructs, label it correctly, and analyse it promptly. I'll document her oxygen therapy or device and the FiO2 at the time of sampling.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What complications are you looking for?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'll apply firm pressure until it's stopped bleeding, dispose of the sharp safely straight away, and check the site and her hand's circulation afterwards.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Perform an arterial blood gas from the radial artery.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'll confirm her identity and explain why we need the gas — to look at her oxygenation and ventilation given the breathlessness — and check she's happy to go ahead.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Would you do an Allen test first?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd check anticoagulation and local contraindications. A formal Allen test isn't universally required if collateral circulation looks clinically adequate — I'd follow local policy rather than treat it as a fixed rule.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd reposition her wrist and re-palpate rather than needle blindly, and adjust my approach before attempting puncture.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd stop, reassess my landmarks, and ask a senior colleague to try or to supervise rather than keep attempting it myself.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Pulse oximetry doesn't detect hypercapnia, and the gas can only be interpreted properly if we know her inspired oxygen and SpO2 at the time of sampling.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: If she were anticoagulated I'd hold pressure for longer, and once the result is back I'd interpret it alongside her clinical picture rather than in isolation.

failures.consequence: Breaches the patient's right to agree to the procedure and undermines trust.
Risks a needlestick injury to the candidate or others.

failures.move: Sending an unlabelled sample or omitting the oxygen device.
failures.consequence: The result may be rejected, or misinterpreted without knowing the inspired oxygen.

failures.move: Repeatedly puncturing the artery without seeking help.
failures.consequence: Causes unnecessary pain, bruising and risks arterial or nerve injury.
Risks bleeding, haematoma and compromise of the distal circulation.

recovery.when: You blank on what to check first
recovery.line: I'd like to structure this around immediate safety, assessment, escalation and definitive management.

recovery.when: Challenged on skipping the Allen test
recovery.line: That wouldn't exclude an adequate collateral circulation, because I'd still assess it clinically and follow local policy before deciding.

knowledge.fact: Confirm identity, indication and consent, and check anticoagulation/bleeding risk before radial puncture.
Do not pull back forcefully on a self-filling blood-gas syringe; let it fill from arterial pressure.
Document the oxygen therapy/device and FiO2 at the time of sampling; pulse oximetry does not detect hypercapnia.
Dispose of sharps safely at the point of use.

recall.think: Bleeding/haematoma and distal neurovascular compromise after puncture.
recall.say: "I'll confirm identity and consent, and check bleeding risk before I start."
do: Aseptic puncture, let the syringe self-fill
Pressure to haemostasis, safe sharps disposal

numbers.value: SpO2 target 94-98% (88-92% if at risk of hypercapnic failure)
numbers.meaning: Target range to document alongside the gas
Year of the UK regulations requiring safe sharps handling and disposal

recall.trap: Assuming pulse oximetry alone excludes CO2 retention.
recall.finish: Prompt analysis and documentation, interpreted alongside the clinical picture.

sources.name: Resuscitation Council UK. The ABCDE Approach
sources.supports: Recording inspired oxygen concentration and SpO2; pulse oximetry does not detect hypercapnia; oxygen saturation targets 94-98% (88-92% if at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure)

partner.opening: Ms Harmsworth, 69, has worsening breathlessness. "Perform an arterial blood gas from the radial artery and talk me through it."

reveals.finding: No anticoagulants; no known bleeding disorder; no local contraindication at either wrist.
Radial pulse is easily palpable at the wrist crease, regular.
She is on 2 L/min via nasal cannulae, SpO2 91% at the time of sampling.

push.question: Would you do an Allen test before this?
push.expect: Not treated as a fixed rule; assess collateral circulation clinically and follow local policy.

push.question: What if you can't feel the pulse well?
push.expect: Reposition the wrist and re-palpate rather than needling blindly.

push.question: What if the syringe won't fill?
push.expect: Do not pull back forcefully; reassess needle position or try again rather than forcing it.

push.question: What must be recorded with the sample?
push.expect: Oxygen therapy/device and FiO2 at the time of sampling, alongside patient identity and time.

curveballs.prompt: She says she's needle-phobic and anxious.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Acknowledge the anxiety, explain each step before doing it, and offer to pause if needed, without skipping consent or safety checks.

curveballs.prompt: You miss the artery on the first attempt.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Stop, reassess landmarks, and try again carefully or ask for senior help rather than repeatedly puncturing blindly.

curveballs.prompt: The sample has visible air bubbles.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Expel the air promptly and remix the sample before analysis, as bubbles distort the result.
Apply pressure for longer after the puncture and monitor the site closely before leaving her.
